def count_reverse_greater(n):
    """Count integers x with 1 <= x <= n whose decimal reversal is strictly
    greater than x.

    The decimal reversal rev(x) of a positive integer x is the integer
    obtained by reading the decimal digits of x from right to left; zeros
    at the end of x become leading zeros and vanish.  For example
    rev(345) = 543, rev(1200) = 21, rev(7) = 7.

    Input domain: n is an int with 1 <= n <= 10**18.  A correct solution
    must be far faster than iterating over 1..n (the bound makes any
    per-number scan astronomically slow).

    Returns a single int: the number of x in [1, n] with rev(x) > x.

    Edge cases: one-digit numbers and palindromes have rev(x) == x and are
    never counted; any x ending in 0 has rev(x) < x and is never counted.
    There is no tie-breaking: the answer is a plain count.

    >>> count_reverse_greater(100)
    36
    >>> count_reverse_greater(1000)
    396
    >>> count_reverse_greater(123456)
    65272
    """
